The Pitch Control Function (PCF) mathematically encodes the tactical duopoly between attackers and defenders. It maps continuous space (pitch coordinates) to discrete possession outcomes (ball control). Crucially, PCF fails when attackers are perfectly balanced, leading to indeterminate possession. To avoid anti-collinearity, we regularize with defender velocity, ensuring stable telemetry. This operator bridges micro-tactical analysis (player positioning) to macro-strategic outcomes (possession loss), making it a foundational sovereign primitive for both GSI's predictive inference and GSE's state-transition models.
